title: Malicious service creation and PowerShell execution on WORKSTATION6
summary: An attacker logged into WORKSTATION6 from internal IP 172.18.39.5, installed a malicious service (PGUJLOAKFQFVOMHGFQPX) that launched PowerShell with an encoded command. The command disabled script block logging and AMSI, then downloaded and executed code from external IP 10.10.10.5. User pgustavo normally uses WORKSTATION5, making this anomalous.
evidence: pgustavo logged into WORKSTATION6 from 172.18.39.5 at 06:57:47.857 (network logon)
Service PGUJLOAKFQFVOMHGFQPX installed by pgustavo at 06:57:48.992 with powershell -enc flag
Decoded command disables Script Block Logging and AMSI, downloads from http://10.10.10.5, runs downloaded code
PowerShell connected to 172.18.39.6 then to 10.10.10.5:80 at 06:57:51.453
User pgustavo normally operates from WORKSTATION5, not WORKSTATION6
Process chain: login -> service install -> cmd.exe -> powershell.exe -> whoami.exe

recommended_actions.action: Isolate WORKSTATION6 from network immediately
Terminate malicious service PGUJLOAKFQFVOMHGFQPX
Block IP 10.10.10.5 at perimeter firewall
Reset pgustavo's credentials and investigate lateral movement to WORKSTATION5
Restore Script Block Logging settings if modified

title: Encoded PowerShell execution on WORKSTATION6 with defense evasion and C2 communication
summary: On WORKSTATION6, services.exe spawned cmd.exe which launched PowerShell with a base64-encoded command. The decoded payload disables Script Block Logging, bypasses AMSI antivirus, and downloads malware from external IP 10.10.10.5 (suspicious, not in company network). This continues the attack chain from ALERT-001 involving malicious service creation.
evidence: Encoded PowerShell command (-enc flag) launched by cmd.exe as child of services.exe on WORKSTATION6
Decoded command disables Script Block Logging and bypasses AMSI (T1562.001)
Downloads from IP 10.10.10.5 flagged as suspicious, not in company network ranges (T1105)
Process chain: services.exe → cmd.exe → powershell.exe (T1059.001)
IP reputation: 10.10.10.5 suspicious, private address outside known company network
related_to_prior: Continues attack chain from ALERT-001 (malicious service creation and PowerShell execution on same host)

recommended_actions.action: Isolate WORKSTATION6 from network immediately
Terminate powershell.exe and parent processes
Block outbound connections to 10.10.10.5 at firewall/proxy
Full malware scan of WORKSTATION6 with updated definitions
Review and restore any modified security settings (Script Block Logging, AMSI)
Investigate origin of services.exe spawning cmd.exe

title: C2 Beacon on WORKSTATION6 with Encoded PowerShell and Defense Evasion
summary: On WORKSTATION6, an encoded PowerShell command (-enc) was executed by cmd.exe (which was spawned by services.exe) as SYSTEM user. The decoded command disables Script Block Logging and AMSI (T1562.001), downloads and runs code from the internet (T1105), and communicates with C2 server 10.10.10.5:80 (T1071.001). The destination IP is suspicious as it's outside company network ranges. This is part of an ongoing attack chain following ALERT-001 and ALERT-002 on the same host.
evidence: powershell.exe executed as SYSTEM with -enc flag connecting to 10.10.10.5:80
decoded command disables Script Block Logging and AMSI to impair defenses
IP 10.10.10.5 flagged as suspicious - private address not in company network ranges
process chain: services.exe -> cmd.exe -> powershell.exe (encoded) -> whoami.exe
decoded command downloads and executes remote code
alert continues pattern from ALERT-001 and ALERT-002 on WORKSTATION6
related_to_prior: Continuation of attack chain from ALERT-001 (malicious service creation) and ALERT-002 (encoded PowerShell execution) on WORKSTATION6

recommended_actions.action: Isolate WORKSTATION6 from network immediately
Terminate all powershell and cmd processes on WORKSTATION6
Block outbound connections to 10.10.10.5 at firewall/proxy
Collect full process memory and disk artifacts from WORKSTATION6 for forensic analysis
Reset credentials for any accounts that may have been compromised via this C2 session
Review and restore any Group Policy changes made by the encoded script (Script Block Logging, AMSI settings)

title: Legitimate Azure Guest Agent lsass access on WORKSTATION5
summary: CollectGuestLogs.exe, a legitimate Microsoft Azure Guest Agent component, opened lsass.exe with memory-read access as part of normal guest log collection. The process chain (WaAppAgent.exe → CollectGuestLogs.exe → conhost.exe → cmd.exe) and command-line parameters (-Mode:ga -FileName:...) are consistent with expected Azure Agent behavior, not credential theft.
evidence: CollectGuestLogs.exe is a legitimate Microsoft Azure Guest Agent component at C:\WindowsAzure\GuestAgent_2.7.41491.993_2020-09-17_150914\
Process chain shows WaAppAgent.exe as parent, then CollectGuestLogs.exe spawning conhost.exe and cmd.exe normally
Command line includes legitimate Azure parameters: -Mode:ga -FileName:C:\WindowsAzure\CollectGuestLogsTemp\73d22eaa-ee60-4181-b12d-9037b2b2c176.zip
Running as SYSTEM user which is typical for Azure Agent operations
No other malicious indicators found in the process timeline
related_to_prior: Alert is on WORKSTATION5, separate from the WORKSTATION6 attack chain in ALERT-001/002/003 (true positives involving malicious service creation, encoded PowerShell, and C2 beacon)

recommended_actions.action: No containment needed - legitimate Azure Agent activity
Verify Azure Guest Agent version and behavior is expected in environment
Continue monitoring WORKSTATION6 alerts (ALERT-001/002/003) for the active attack chain
